title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff during regional failover + load-shedding
author: Aisha Patel
description: This hotfix addresses a production issue observed during a partial regional outage where the SLO enforcer entered a backoff/thrashing cycle and aggressively triggered load-shedding, causing increased error surface and latency for latency-sensitive routes. Root cause: edge-case in the enforcer's backoff ordering and hysteresis when regional failover signals overlap with transient client-side timeouts. The enforcer would reset backoff state in the wrong order when failover events and internal circuit-breaker transitions happened concurrently, which under sustained elevated load produced cascading shed decisions. Fixes in this PR: 1) Correct ordering and guards in the backoff/hysteresis state machine so failover transitions do not reset active in-flight buckets incorrectly; 2) Introduce a jittered exponential backoff with upper bound and configurable hysteresis windows to prevent rapid toggling; 3) Decrease default aggressiveness of load-shedding thresholds during detected regional failover and add a short grace period for warm-up after failover; 4) Add additional metrics and tracing hooks (slo_enforcer.backoff_state, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_count, slo_enforcer.last_failover_ts) to make incidents visible; 5) Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent failover+timeout signals and ensure no thrashing; 6) Add a migration-safe config flag (slo_enforcer.stable_backoff_v2) so the change can be toggled in Dedicated/Private rollouts. Checklist: - [x] Fix state machine ordering and add guards - [x] Implement jittered backoff and hysteresis window - [x] Add metrics + tracing - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Update docs/operational runbook - [x] Add rollout plan and migration flag - [x] Smoke-tested in perf-canary region This is a targeted hotfix (low-risk API changes, runtime-only) intended to be cherry-picked to the active release branch if necessary.

Prevents rapid backoff/hysteresis thrashing that could trigger aggressive load-shedding under concurrent failover and client-timeout signals.
